problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨2,3,-1⟩+t⟨-1,2,3⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨-2,1,4⟩=11.
$$
worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨2-t,3+2t,-1+3t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨2-t,3+2t,-1+3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨-2,1,4⟩ & =11 \\ ⟨2-t,3+2t,-1+3t⟩\cdot ⟨-2,1,4⟩ & =11 \\ -2(2-t)+1(3+2t)+4(-1+3t) & =11 \\ -4+2t+3+2t-4+12t & =11 \\ 16t & =16 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=1$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨2-1,3+2(1),-1+3(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,5,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(1,5,2).$
